HardwareNote: Cobalt 200 Arm64 pod (temp_ef_azure_server_al3 10.1.4.6 / temp_ef_azure_client 10.1.4.7). The server is a ~128-core machine; cobalt100 was 4 cores. The application is confined to 4 cores with --application.cpuSet 0-3 so that core count is held constant and the comparison isolates the hardware generation. Verified: derived cores (benchmarks/cpu/raw / benchmarks/cpu) = 4.0, identical to cobalt100.
SaturationNote: Unconstrained, this pod cannot be saturated by the single available load client: 256 conns -> 1.69M rps at 74% server CPU; 1024 -> 3.02M at 80% server / 81% client; 4096 -> 3.71M at 80% server / 99% client. Measurements would have been partly client-bound. Under cpuSet 0-3 the server runs at 93% CPU with the client at 9%, so the app is the bottleneck and the four-arm deltas are valid.
PinNote: Same pins as local-bits-r3-arm64.json, deliberately: the software stack must be byte-identical to the cobalt100 run for the hardware comparison to mean anything. Published-size canary 144,025 KB confirmed identical on cobalt200.
CoresVarNote: The profile keeps cores: 16 -- the same stale value cobalt100 carried -- because `cores` feeds concurrencyPerHttpClient in httpclient.benchmarks.yml. Changing it would alter load generation and add a second variable. It does not reflect real core count.
ScenarioNote: No db agent exists on this pod, so fortunes / fortunes_ef / multiple_queries cannot run. json, plaintext and mvc are the usable set -- the same set that was reliable on cobalt100.
